q: In Calvin's 'lollipop' experiments, algae given 14CO2 for only ~5 seconds and then killed in hot methanol had most of the label in glycerate-3-phosphate (GP). What does this show?
options: CO2 is first converted directly into glucose, which is then broken down further into GP
GP is the first stable product of carbon fixation, formed when Rubisco adds CO2 to RuBP
Triose phosphate is the first product of carbon fixation, and GP is only made from it later
RuBP is synthesised from CO2 in a single step, then converted directly into GP
explanation: By shortening exposure times and separating compounds by chromatography and autoradiography, Calvin traced the order of labelling: GP first, then triose phosphate, hexoses and later RuBP – revealing the cycle. Hot methanol stopped all enzyme reactions instantly. Rubisco carboxylates RuBP (5C) to an unstable 6C intermediate that splits into two GP (3C).
